video_title: Luka's MESSAGE to Lebron | Former NBA Ref TELLS ALL

quotes.speaker: Byron Scott
quotes.summary_phrase: Luka Doncic's 'It feels great' comment about LeBron James leaving
quotes.excerpt: It feels great, I'm ready to go.

text_blocks.speaker: Byron Scott
text_blocks.text: Luka did not say, 'I'm happy LeBron is gone,' but when somebody says, 'LeBron's gone, this is your team, how does that feel?' and your first three words are, 'It feels great,' did Luka just actually say the quiet part out loud?

text_blocks.speaker: Derek Richardson
text_blocks.text: I don't think he meant it feels great that LeBron's gone and this is my team. He said, 'I've been in this position before where it's been his team,' so to speak. I don't think Luka meant anything by that as far as throwing a shot at LeBron.

quotes.speaker: Derek Richardson
quotes.summary_phrase: LeBron James' departure creates pressure for the Lakers' young core
quotes.excerpt: LeBron kind of covered up a lot of things for guys because you could always throw it on him.

text_blocks.speaker: Derek Richardson
text_blocks.text: LeBron kind of covered up a lot of things for guys because you could always throw it on him. Now, it's his chance to really show what he's made of because you don't have that excuse anymore. It's all about what can you guys do, whether it's Luka, Austin Reaves, or Walker Kessler. There's a lot of pressure on this Lakers team.

text_blocks.speaker: Byron Scott
text_blocks.text: If you look at it from a coach's perspective, how do you think Luka should perceive now him being the man? The thing about being the man and being the greatest player on your team, or being a player that's one of the greatest players in the league, they're all two-way players. That's the biggest difference.

quotes.speaker: Derek Richardson
quotes.summary_phrase: Luka Doncic needs accountability to succeed without LeBron James
quotes.excerpt: What he needs is accountability. Who's going to hold him accountable when he's doing that stuff?

text_blocks.speaker: Derek Richardson
text_blocks.text: Luka's always had freedom. He'd come up and shoot that three, and LeBron tried to play it off, but I could tell he was a little pissed. Luka's always had the freedom. What he needs is accountability. Who's going to hold him accountable when he's doing that stuff? Because you got to know, your teammates need to have the ball too, and they got to be comfortable and be willing to help you and everything else.

text_blocks.speaker: Byron Scott
text_blocks.text: Even last year, LeBron took a step back to allow him to do what he does. So the freedom ain't the question. We are basketball people up here. Go back in history, teams that win championships, they are always in the top five in the NBA in defensive efficiency as well. They ain't in the middle, they ain't in the 20s, they in the top five. So if they really want to win a championship this year, a lot of it is going to be put on Luka's shoulder because he's the franchise player.

quotes.speaker: Derek Richardson
quotes.summary_phrase: LeBron James' comments about wanting to finish his career in New York
quotes.excerpt: I didn't leave my family to lose in the second round.
quotes.quote: He's sitting there as a Sixer and reveals that he had visions of finishing his career playing at Madison Square Garden and then tells Philadelphia, 'I didn't leave my family to lose in the second round.' There is a lot there to unzip.

quotes.speaker: Derek Richardson
quotes.summary_phrase: LeBron James' transparency about his future plans
quotes.excerpt: Sometimes we want to show that we're transparent and sometimes we're too transparent.

text_blocks.speaker: Derek Richardson
text_blocks.text: I think it has to do with the fact that he's going to be living in both cities, so he's trying to be nice, I guess. I don't know, but I agree with you. It's like sometimes we want to show that we're transparent and sometimes we're too transparent, and I think he felt trapped to that. You don't have to give us everything because it feels so backhanded, not only to the Knicks but to Philadelphia.

text_blocks.speaker: Byron Scott
text_blocks.text: Giving him the benefit of the doubt, technically it was Rich Paul who told somebody that LeBron would have played in New York if the Knicks wouldn't have won, and somebody in the media asked LeBron the question and he just clarified it.

quotes.speaker: Derek Richardson
quotes.summary_phrase: Derek Richardson on the difficulty of officiating stars like Buck Williams and Karl Malone
quotes.excerpt: I had to deal with Buck Williams, Karl Malone, Oakley.
quotes.quote: When I first came in, it was cosmopolitan. I had to deal with Buck Williams, Karl Malone, Oakley, to a dope male, every single game. And now you have a lot of the league is a lot younger, and the challenge for me, when I think about it and I talk to some of my former colleagues, I'm like, 'Man, we got to understand, these guys have been officiated by high school officials a lot longer than they've been officiated by us.'

quotes.speaker: Derek Richardson
quotes.summary_phrase: Derek Richardson on the influence of Hugh Hollins on his career
quotes.excerpt: The first person I have to acknowledge is Hugh Hollins.
quotes.quote: The first person I have to acknowledge is Hugh Hollins. Hugh Hollins came from the neighborhood, he came down to the Crenshaw League, and he would mentor me and my best friend Rodney Mott, tell us the things that we needed to do in order to move up. And both Rodney and I were in our 30s. You have officials now being hired in their mid-20s, so we're almost out of the game when we came in.

quotes.speaker: Derek Richardson
quotes.summary_phrase: Derek Richardson on the lack of personality in modern NBA officiating
quotes.excerpt: I don't see that anymore. I just see a bunch of robotic individuals.

text_blocks.speaker: Derek Richardson
text_blocks.text: I came in in 1987, and the one thing I've always noticed and remembered about the referees is that most of them had a personality. Now that I look at the NBA, I don't see that anymore. I just see a bunch of robotic individuals making calls, very stoic, and they don't even engage anymore. We used to have conversations, because it was a welcome thing, as long as you came at a ref in the right way.

text_blocks.speaker: Byron Scott
text_blocks.text: Is that something that the NBA consciously thought about is bringing these guys, or are they just hiring guys without personalities?

quotes.speaker: Derek Richardson
quotes.summary_phrase: Derek Richardson on the importance of personality in officiating
quotes.excerpt: He's not bringing anybody on the team that could not play.
quotes.quote: He's not bringing anybody on the team that could not play. It was, I don't care if it was his son. You got, and so everyone that's hired, they can referee, but you have different personalities and you have people that come from different cultures, and do they understand the culture of the NBA?

quotes.speaker: Derek Richardson
quotes.summary_phrase: Derek Richardson on how veteran officials handle young players
quotes.excerpt: I gave Mark Jackson his only technical foul.
quotes.quote: And as a young official, you you're doing everything black and white. Right? Like I said, you know, the speed limit is 55, foul. Right? But then when you you start to understand the game a little bit more, you know, like like six years ago, out of bounds. If we had doubt, we went looked at it. They cut all of that out. Because that was breaking up the flow of the game. And more importantly, you know, we are a form of entertainment. You know, if all of a sudden the young generation, you only got two hours at the max, right? They're gone. So now what are you losing? You losing your your commercial money. And then those 30-second spot commercials are millions and millions of dollars. So you know, the bottom line is, sports is a business. Oh, without a doubt. It's a business and we don't understand that.
